rows.author: I066;
rows.title_full: ESTABLISHMENT OF REHABILITATION CENTERS FOR INDIVIDUALS WHO SURRENDERED TO AUTHORITIES ON DRUG-RELATED ACTIVITIES
rows.abstract:
Rep. Teves spoke about the rehabilitation of the
country´s drug surrenderees, and citing his previous experience as a recovering drug addict, suggested ways of minimizing national government´s cost of drug rehabilitation from P90,000 per addict per program to only P2,500. He said that this could be achieved by doing the programs in public classrooms manned by counselors and volunteers from five o´clock in the afternoon to eight o´clock in the evening as by then, the facilities are no longer used by the
students; allowing 50 drug dependents per classroom for a period of eight to 12 weeks, with follow-up meetings every eight to nine in the morning in the barangays´ covered courts; and providing nine to 10 optional physical therapy activities. Rep. Teves disclosed that he, together with Rep. Albee Benitez, Governor Alfredo Marañon of Negros Occidental, and his brother, former Rep. Pryde Henry A. Teves would soon launch said program in his province. He also discussed the reasons why the Members should consider his proposed modality and be wary of “chopsuey” or mixed modalities as there are various types of drug pushers and users. In closing, he informed the people and those concerned that drug
addiction is a disease and therefore should be covered by the PhilHealth.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.4,pp.72&73)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on DANGEROUS DRUGS since 2016-09-06
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: I049;
rows.title_full: SUPPORT TO THE GOVERNMENT'S CAMPAIGN AGAINST ILLEGAL DRUGS
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Rogelio “Ruel” D.
Pacquiao from the Lone District of Sarangani initially thanked the people of his District for the overwhelming mandate they gave him in the last
elections, as well as the support of his elder brother, Senator Emmanuel “Manny” Pacquiao. He also congratulated Speaker Pantaleon D. Alvarez, a fellow Mindanaoan, as the Speaker of the 17th Congress of the House of Representatives. As a neophyte Member of the House, he said that he has committed himself to perform his constitutional
duty as legislator with utmost integrity, prudence, fidelity, and accountability. He stated that with his humble beginnings and experiences as barangay captain and city councilor, he can articulate the issues and aspirations of the people into meaningful legislative measures.
As one of the poorest provinces in Mindanao, he
cited the poverty issues facing Sarangani in terms of health and nutrition, water and sanitation, basic education, livelihood and income and expressed hope that he could bring these issues in the national level. He also enumerated several of his dreams for the Philippines. After expressing his wholehearted support to the agenda of President Rodrigo Roa Duterte, Rep. Pacquiao urged his colleagues to scrutinize the National Expenditure Program for 2017 and the succeeding years to ensure that substantial budget for
poverty alleviation is allocated for the 20 poorest provinces of the country. In closing, Rep. Pacquiao expressed hope that his concerns will be given preferential attention by the leadership considering that Congress holds the power of the purse.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on DANGEROUS DRUGS since 2016-09-06
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: I090;
rows.title_full: RIGHT TO LIFE
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. H. Harry L. Roque
Jr. from Party-List Kabayan rose to clarify certain basic principles that must serve as important pillars of any society. Initially, he said that he supports many of President Duterte´s economic and social programs for the least of the people, but averred that he wished to confront some assertions in the President´s SONA
considering that he had been fighting for the
recognition of societal values, in his professional life in the last two decades or so. He pointed out that there were contradicting statements in the President´s SONA with regard to human rights and the rule of law. He underscored the President´s promise to uplift the conditions of the common tao but has also launched a bloody drug war where the dead bodies piling up mostly come from the same poor throng to whom he
had promised economic and social salvation.
Concurring with his former Professor in International Law, Dame Rosalyn Higgins, regarding the universality of the human spirit, Rep. Roque
elaborated on what her words meant for him, that the need for the recognition of fundamental rights is universal, regardless of culture, religion or nationality. He maintained that if law and order is important to development, so are civil and political freedoms and explained that foundational rights anticipate all other rights which, meanwhile, are inconceivable and meaningless without foundational rights. Rep. Roque (H.) then condemned the extrajudicial killing of journalists because it permanently denied their right to free expression pointing out the Maguindanao Massacre being described by the international organizations as the single worst attack on press freedom. He castigated the failure of the justice system to defend and protect the victims of human rights violations and asked what former Justice Secretary Leila de Lima had done to address the culture of impunity in the Philippines as exemplified
in the Maguindanao Massacre. He stressed that the
new task force President Duterte recently created to investigate such killings might go the way of its predecessors without the vigorous investigation and successful prosecution of cases. He suggested the overhaul of the criminal justice system and the enactment of laws to put into effect the long-standing Minnesota Protocol, or the Manual on the Effective Prevention and Investigation of Extra-Legal, Arbitrary, and Summary Executions. Subsequently, Rep. Roque (H.) discussed the responsibility of the State for human rights and humanitarian law. He explained how, in the international legal system, the State is the primary domestic institution charged with the task of ensuring the promotion and protection of human rights especially in view of its obligations under treaties. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.4,pp.73-74)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2016-09-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Atienza, Lagman and Bataoil.

rows.author: I080;
rows.title_full: RESUMPTION OF PEACE TALKS BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENT AND THE NATIONAL DEMOCRATIC FRONT OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Resumption Of The Peace Talks Between C P P / N P A / N D F And The G R P
rows.abstract:
At the outset, Rep. Casilao congratulated President Rodrigo Roa Duterte for delivering his first Stateof-the-Nation Address (SONA) and commended Speaker Pantaleon D. Alvarez and the House leadership and Secretariat for successfully hosting the meaningful and historic SONA. He also commended the 3,000-strong Lumad, Moro and farmer contingents from Mindanao who joined the week-long caravan to Manila in support of the progressive policies promised by President Duterte. Thereupon, Rep. Casilao spoke on the issue of the resumption of the peace talks between the National Democratic Front of the Philippines (NDFP) and the government especially on matters pertaining to social
economic reforms which is crucial in solving the root causes of the more than four-decades of armed conflict between the government and the CPP-NPA-NDF. He stressed that he had personally witnessed the rights of the farmers and Lumads to their lands being violently repressed by past administrations and counterinsurgency operations that led to massive militarization, extrajudicial killings, evacuation, and other forms of human rights violations. As such, he said that they remain on the positive outlook of expressing support on the resumption of the formal peace talks set on August 20, 2016 in Oslo, Norway even though President Duterte declared the lifting of the ceasefire agreement. As militarization and abuses against the people continue especially among the Lumad and farmer communities, Rep. Casilao enjoined the Members to support 1) the peace agreement between the NDFP and the government especially the socioeconomic reform
agenda on agrarian reform, national industrialization, wage and land reform for the indigenous peoples (IPs), and 2) the effort to release all political prisoners, including the NDFP consultants, which is a very important factor in building a more favorable condition for the success of the peace negotiation. He expressed hope that the Duterte Administration can play an active and significant role in the pursuit of
peace in the country. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.5,p.48)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2016-09-06

rows.author: I010;
rows.title_short: Crusade Against Illegal Drugs / Railway System
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bordado, in rejoicing over the President´s
crusade against illegal drugs and program to overhaul the Philippine railways system, among other things, expressed support thereto but emphasized the need to put in place systems and mechanisms to protect innocent and helpless people. He also underscored how the Philippine National Railways, which is vital to the development of his region, has remained in perpetual state of disrepair despite the huge amount of money that the national government
has allocated for its rehabilitation in the past.
As he commended the President for “walking the
extra mile” in his efforts to solve the insurgency problem, he reiterated his support for the Administration´s goal of achieving progress and peace through legislative measures. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.5,p48)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-08-02

rows.author: I102;
rows.title_full: REACTION TO PRESIDENT DUTERTE'S SONA STATEMENT THAT THE PARTY-LIST SYSTEM HAS BEEN ABUSED AND HAS BECOME A MOCKERY OF THE LAW
rows.title_short: Partylist As A Mockery Of The Law
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Bondoc,
Rep. Salvador B. Belaro Jr. from Party-List 1-
Ang Edukasyon focused on President Duterte´s recent statement that the party-list system has been abused and has become a mockery of the law. He noted that said comment was followed by ascerbic bashings of the system in Facebook and social media that prompted supporters of his party-list group to issue a statement in defense of its members. He added that on behalf of 1-Ang Edukasyon Party-List, he took exception to the President´s opinion and stressed that his
party-list group´s presence in Congress is not a mockery of the law. This, as he underscored the following points: 1) around 278,693 Filipinos voted for his party-list organization because they believe in its intention and platform in the field of education; 2) the party-list system is an equalizing measure and a legal innovation in sync with the democratization of power and promotion of social justice; 3) his group´s nominees
in the last party-list elections were self-made persons who are pillars of the education sector; and 4) he had filed 30 bills and resolutions fostering, empowering, and protecting education, among others. He then urged his fellow party-list Representatives to respond accordingly to what he referred to as “a crisis in the image of the party-list system in general,” by 1) educating the public on the importance of the system, 2) showcasing its accomplishments thus far; and 3) raising the bar of what previous party-list
groups in Congress have done.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.5,p.49)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2016-09-06

rows.author: I105;
rows.title_full: NEED FOR THE PROPER IMPLEMENTATION OF THE \"ANTI-DRUNK AND DRUGGED DRIVING LAW\"
rows.abstract:
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Jose Antonio
“Kuya Jonathan” R. Sy-Alvarado from the First District of Bulacan called for the proper implementation of Republic Act No. 10586 also known as the “AntiDrunk and Drugged Driving Act of 2013.” This, as he cited statistics and reports on road safety and road accidents due to drunk driving or driving under the influence of drugs and similar substances; mentioned recent newspaper reports on road safety and road rage; and informed his colleagues of a vehicular accident involving
him and a policeman in Calumpit, Bulacan which required him to wear a neck brace for at least
five months. As he called on the people to faithfully adhere to the road safety laws in order to save lives, he likewise seek stiffer penalties for those who will violate the law. As such, he asked that he be allowed to be a coauthor of House Bill No. 5, amending RA No. 10586 to impose higher penalties for violations thereof. With the reported increase in number of accidents
related to alcohol intoxication and drugs, Rep. Sy-Alvarado earnestly appealed on the need for government to strengthen its advocacy on road safety to lessen the deaths attributed to drunk or drugged driving. 
(SOURCE: HOuse Journal No.5,p.49)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2016-09-06

rows.author: H081;
rows.title_full: SCRAPPING OF THE ENHANCED DEFENSE COOPERATION AGREEMENT (EDCA)
rows.title_short: Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement ( E D C A )
rows.abstract:
Rep. Zarate delved into the Enhanced Defense
Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) which Bayan Muna
and other nationalist organizations have wanted to be scrapped. He said that EDCA is not good for the country because this would only open the Philippines to America for their use in any way they wish. He further said that EDCA will give American troops the power to stay permanently on the agreed locations on rotational basis. This, he averred, would just bring back the American bases to the country which the Filipinos had fought for to be ousted. Rep. Zarate pointed out that the nullification of EDCA will be a big challenge for President Duterte´s Administration who had said earlier on that he would only recognize treaties in accordance with the people´s welfare. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.5,p.49)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2016-09-06

rows.author: G003;
rows.title_full: SUPPORT TO PRESIDENT DUTERTE'S PROMISE TO END LABOR CONTRACTUALIZATION
rows.abstract:
Rep. Aglipay-Villar, in joining President Duterte
in his fight to end contractualization schemes that rob workers of their rights promised them under the Constitution and under the Labor Code, said that she will continue the fight against rampant exploitative contractualization schemes that undermine the dignity of workers. At the start of her first term as the Representative
of DIWA Party-List, she stated that she made the end of labor contractualization as her priority because it was being used to circumvent the worker´s constitutionally enshrined right to security of tenure. She added that the bill she filed in the 15th and the 16th Congress to correct the loopholes in the Labor Code to end such constitutional practice, was approved only up to the Committee level and that she would re-file it in the present Congress. After citing the fact that more than one-third of the labor force are not regular employees, Rep. Aglipay discussed the three forms of exploitative contractualization
that demand redress, namely, labor only
contracting, fixed-term employment, and the
abuse of the probationary status of workers. She proposed to change the legal framework for employment by adopting several measures such as limiting fixed term contracts or automatic termination and invalidating the termination of probationary employees when done to prevent security of tenure. She explained, however, that she did not intend to do away with fixed-term employment or job contracting but only to clarify which jobs may be legitimately contracted out
and which ones should be done by regular workers.
To conclude, Rep. Aglipay asked her colleagues
to work for the plight of the labor force because securing their jobs is securing the future of the nation. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.5,p.50)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2016-09-06

rows.author: G105;
rows.title_full: WOMEN'S PLIGHT
rows.abstract:
Next recognized by the Chair upon Rep. Tugna´s
motion, Rep. Emmi A. De Jesus from the Party-List
Gabriela stressed that the state of women reflects the true state of a nation. Speaking in Filipino, she discussed the plight of this sector which includes issues of low wages, demolition, and lack of job opportunities and basic services in relocation centers. She reminded the Members about President Duterte´s pronouncements regarding the uplifting of the people´s welfare as she informed them of a women´s summit that was recently held in Davao that came up with a comprehensive agenda summed up in the word “CHANGE”. She then explained what each letter of the word “Change” stood for and stressed the mandate of her Party-List which is for the advancement of women and that they would fight any abuse against them. She stated that it is their vision that in the next
SONA and especially in the coming State of the
Women Address, the welfare of women would be addressed.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.5,p.50)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2016-09-06

rows.author: I078;
rows.title_full: DISAGREEMENT WITH PLAN TO LOWER THE AGE OF CRIMINAL RESPONSIBILITY OF CHILDREN
rows.abstract:
As a child rights advocate, Rep. Brosas spoke on
the issue of lowering the age of criminal responsibility wherein she discussed the economic aspect and social behavior of youth offenders. As she cited the position of the Psychological Association of the Philippines, the SalinLahi Alliance for Children´s Concern, and the Philippine Action for Youth Offenders, she
pointed out that lowering the age of criminal responsibility to nine years old has no basis and would be making the situation worse and would create a far bleaker and darker future for the generations to come. She stressed that youth offenders should be looked at as victims and not as criminals. As such and as the Philippines is a signatory to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, Rep. Brosas enjoined her colleagues to probe into the implementation of the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act and to help strengthen the government´s capacity to respond to the problem of youth offenders by establishing
more halfway homes and empowering social
workers on the ground before putting the blame on the children themselves. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.5,pp.50-51)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2016-09-06

rows.author: I096;
rows.title_full: DEFENDED THE PARTY-LIST SYSTEM
rows.abstract:
In reaction to the President´s statement the previous week as quoted by the media that he would abolish the party-list system of representation in Congress under a new Constitution, Rep. Villarin emphasized the system´s composition and major role in the pursuit of political and electoral reforms as provided by the 1987 Constitution, particularly with respect to the minority parties vis-Ã -vis the traditionally dominant parties, and the representation of the various marginalized sectors. As he underscored how the party-list system has benefitted the people through bills and resolutions that are of national in scope and sectoral in representation, he however noted the rise of new party-list groups and the need to get into the winning circle because of increasing
cost of campaign. He suggested that Congress
look into the merits of enacting a comprehensive
campaign finance law and amending the Party-List
System Act, this as he concluded that abolishing the party-list system is out of the question.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. LAGMAN
Thereafter, on motion of Rep. Bondoc, the Chair
recognized Rep. Lagman, who initially opined that the party-list system should not be consigned to the killing fields but instead strengthened and given perfecting amendments to put premium to its original concept of helping the marginalized and underrepresented sectors through a representation in Congress. To the queries of Rep. Lagman, Rep. Villarin agreed that a number of decisions rendered by the Supreme Court were inconsistent with each other; with regard to the Supreme Court decision on Atong Paglaum case, that the second group known as lacking in well-defined political constituencies was not actually a separate group because the phrase “lacking well defined
political constituencies” refers to the marginalized and underrepresented sectors; that there is only one group entitled to party-list representation and these are the marginalized and underrepresented sectors which do not have well-defined political constituencies. In closing his interpellation, Rep. Lagman thanked Rep. Villarin and opined that instead of abolishing the party-list system, Congress should introduce perfecting amendments to the existing law. Moreover, he proposed that the Members should review
the ambivalent and conflicting decisions of the
Supreme Court. Rep. Villarin agreed therewith and
said that he fully supports Rep. Lagman´s proposition.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.5,p.51)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2016-09-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Lagman

rows.author: I062;
rows.title_full: SUPPORT TO AMENDING THE CONSTITUTION THROUGH CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Bondoc, the Chair recognized
Rep. Edgar Mary S. Sarmiento from the First District of Samar who defended the Members of the 17th Congress from their alleged incompetence to amend the Constitution. Speaking in Filipino, he said that they participated in the House-conducted executive course on legislation, were knowledgeable about the shortcomings of government, were exposed to the problems and concerns of their constituencies, and possessed integrity and heart and had the best interest
of the people in mind. He explained that a new Constitution was necessary in view of the changing socioeconomic indicators and that the same would still be subject to a plebiscite. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.6,pp.25-26)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS since 2016-09-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Atienza and Veloso (V.)

rows.author: H057;
rows.title_full: NEED TO PASS A GENUINE FREEDOM OF INFORMATION BILL
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tambunting cited the importance of the
freedom of information by highlighting the following points: it is the very essence of democracy; it enables the people to participate in the decision-making process of government; it allows them to monitor and check any abuses of power or wrongdoing by leaders whom they have elected in office; and it helps the people prevent government officials from committing the wrongdoings at the expense and detriment of
the people they vowed to serve. He pointed out that freedom of information is so important that it has been enshrined in the 1973 and 1987 Constitutions both of which recognize the right of access of the people to matters of public concern and guarantee the right of the people to access official records, documents, papers pertaining to official acts, transactions, decisions and research data used as basis for policy development. Although there were laws passed to
make available information needed by the public or
the courts, he disclosed that these laws had not been effective in curbing the commission of anomalous transactions in government. It is for this reason, he said, that he had filed the Freedom of Information Bill in the 16th Congress but he lamented that the Members failed to pass it on time maybe for more urgent and pressing reasons. He then informed the Body that on June 30, 2016, he had reintroduced House Bill No. 126 or the Freedom of Information Bill which would help President Rodrigo Roa Duterte achieve his goal of alleviating if not eradicating poverty in the country by attracting international and local investments in the country. He expressed hope that the Members, through further debates, deliberations and requisite public hearings, would come out with a law that includes all essential elements of a genuine Freedom of Information Law. Considering that the President announced during his SONA that he had signed and issued an executive order requiring public disclosure
of documents related to government transactions,
assets, liabilities and net worth of government officials, and other documents to media and the public, subject to certain conditions such as national security and others, he said that the President needs the help and support of the Legislative and the Judicial branches of government. It is in this light that he would seek the support of the Members in passing
House Bill No. 126 the soonest possible time. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.6,p.29)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2016-08-03

rows.author: I028;
rows.title_full: THE LATE REP. ENRIQUE GARCIA, JR'S VISION OF EMPOWERMENT FOR LGUs: A PRELUDE TO FEDERALISM
rows.abstract:
Rep. Garcia rose to pay homage to his father, the
late former Bataan Congressman and Governor
Enrique “Tet” T. Garcia Jr. or fondly known as 
Congressman Tet. He then related to the Body
Congressman Tet´s tenacity in pursuing worthy
national causes and issues during his tenure as Bataan governor and district representative. One of those issues, he continued, was the gross injustice perpetrated by the national government against local government units (LGUs), especially concerning the implementation of an erroneous provision of the 1991 Local Government Code (LGC) wherein LGUs are getting their Internal Revenue Allotment (IRA) shares in amounts that are much less than what the law provides. He pointed out that it was Congressman Tet who saw, heard and felt the crying need of the LGUs for empowerment and judicial relief and appealed to the government to do what is right and just. He lamented, however, that Congressman Tet´s plea was
ignored and that the government has continued to
retain the funds for its own use, as in the case of the Disbursement Acceleration Program (DAP).
As the new leadership has taken the reign of
government, he cited to the Body his father´s
unspoken message to President Rodrigo Roa Duterte
on the issue of federalism. He stressed that his
father´s vision of empowering the LGUs is the fast
and simple solution to the problem of inequitable
distribution of the country´s national wealth. He then urged President Duterte to direct the Departments of Finance (DOF), Budget and Management (DBM) and the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) to recompute the IRA in accordance with Section 284 of the LGC and relieve the LGUs from awaiting the Supreme Court decision on the IRA petition. In closing, he underscored that said funds due the LGUs will solve underspending that was cited as the reason for the deceleration of the nation´s economic growth.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,pp.43-44)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2016-09-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Sy-Alvarado and Gonzales (A.)

rows.author: H056;
rows.title_full: NEED TO INVESTIGATE DISPARITY IN THE RATES OF WATER FEES PAID BY THE NATIONAL IRRIGATION ADMINISTRATION (NIA) TO CE CASECNAN WATER ENERGY COMPANY, INC.
rows.abstract:
As Rep. Suansing stated with pride that the
Province of Nueva Ecija is known as the rice granary of the Philippines because it is the top producer of rice, onion and other high-value crops. She however lamented the sad plight of the country´s farmers which she said is aggravated by inadequate government support in the areas of microfinancing, research programs, and postharvest facilities. Zeroing in on the heavy burden imposed on farmers through mandatory payment of irrigation
service fees, she thereafter called on the House of Representatives to exercise its oversight functions and investigate the obscenely huge disparity in the rates of water fees paid by the National Irrigation Administration (NIA) to CE Casecnan Water and Energy Company, Inc. and the water fees paid by First Gen to NIA to determine whether the national government is losing revenue from the contracts and agreements entered into by the NIA with these two corporations. She likewise suggested that to improve the country´s agricultural industry, the government should not only level the playing field for the farmers
and farm workers but should also strengthen its
financial support through credit lines and subsidies. In closing, she said that the Members, as the elected Representatives of the people, have the avowed task and solemn obligation to ensure not only the farmer´s well-being but more importantly to protect their right to justice.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7 pp.44-45)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2016-09-06

rows.author: H065;
rows.title_full: NEED TO END THE ILLEGAL USE OF PUBLIC WATERS OF THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Jose L. Atienza Jr.
from Buhay Party-List spoke on the importance of
water to the lives of the people and the worsening
state of bodies of waters such as lakes and rivers in the country. In particular, he discussed the condition of the Laguna de Bay which he said was slowly deteriorating because of over construction of fish pens built by their abusive owners. As he called on the Body to put an end to the illegal use of the country´s public waters, he also informed them that his Party-List Buhay has been crafting measures which would help save the lakes and rivers of the country. Moreover, he asked the support of the Members to make it mandatory that all household structures, and buildings be provided with water catchment facility for the reuse of water; and for LGUs to be responsible for all the water bodies in their respective areas of jurisdiction. With the present government bent on helping fishermen in the country, Rep. Atienza said that Congress should support the efforts of the President so that the present and future generations of Filipinos would benefit from fresh water which is now getting scarce all over the world. He then appealed to his colleagues to give serious attention to the problem of saving the bodies of water in the country. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,p.45)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2016-09-06

rows.author: I091;
rows.title_full: TRANSFORMATION OF BASIC EDUCATION CURRICULUM FROM FOCUS ON SKILLS ON READING, WRITING AND ARITHMETIC, TO DEVELOPING CRITICAL THINKING, CRAFTSMANSHIP AND CHARACTER
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, upon Rep. Tugna´s
motion, Rep. Ron P. Salo from Kabayan Party-List
centered on the relevant laws and meaningful reforms that Congress should craft to address the widespread poverty and arrest the continued degradation of the society. Recalling his recent trip to Switzerland and seeing a village belonging to farmers which he thought was for the rich and famous, Rep. Salo said that upon coming home to the country, he was convinced that with the abundant God-given natural resources of the Philippines, and with the hardworking and patient Filipinos, the Philippines can also be prosperous and become a highly developed country and live comfortably too. He pointed out that this could only be achieved through education because this is the key to the betterment of the society. Rep. Salo underscored that the current basic education curriculum is inadequate to equip the people with the requisite knowledge, skills and values to improve their lives and to get out from the morass
of poverty. He said that while developing the skills on Reading, Writing and Arithmetic are certainly important, he believed that a curriculum that is aimed to develop critical thinking, craftsmanship and character is vital to enable individuals to attain their highest potentials as human beings, and provide them with life skills that will enable them to thrive and not just survive. He thereafter asked his colleagues to support his proposed bill to transform the paradigm of basic education from the 3Rs to the 3Cs and work for the full development of the people and the progress of the nation. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,p.45)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2016-09-06

rows.author: I018;
rows.title_full: NEED FOR ALL MINING COMPANIES TO BE STRICTLY REGULATED AND THAT THE HOST COMMUNITIES MUST BE ENTITLED TO SUBSTANTIAL AND REALISTIC FINANCIAL BENEFITS AND ALLOCATED SUCH BENEFITS UNDER THEIR OWN TERMS
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair upon Rep. Bondoc´s
motion, Rep. Luisa Lloren Cuaresma from the Lone 
District of Nueva Vizcaya spoke about the plight of her constituents who, she said, had suffered too much and too long from the destruction brought by irresponsible mining companies. She discusssed how miners implementing the Didipio Gold and Copper Project in Nueva Vizcaya, which was the first Financial and Technical Assistance Agreement
(FTAA) issued by the government, promised huge
profit and benefits to the local community but
actually caused deforestation, human rights
violations, abuse and harassment of cultural
minorities as well as local leaders including herself when she was provincial governor, evasion and abuse of legal processes and laws, militarization, and the displacement of local residents. She cited how the the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) misinterpreted the 1991 Local Government Code (LGC) on the requirements for construction and development projects, in order to help the miners promote and protect their interests. She explained how FTAAs are very prejudicial to the government and how easily they could be obtained and how miners could arbitrarily enter and possess lands to mine. As destructive, illegal and irresponsible mining should be stopped, Rep. Cuaresma stressed that all mining companies must be strictly regulated and that
the host communities must be entitled to substantial and realistic financial benefits and allocated such benefits under their own terms. She stated that she welcomes and supports President Duterte and DENR Secretary Gina Lopez´ call to end destructive and illegal mining and foster responsible mining in the country. She also welcomes Secretary Lopez´ promise to ask the MGB to cancel the permit of a foreign mining company in Nueva Vizcaya. She then ended her speech by presenting to the Body pictures and videos showing the before-and-after effects of illegal mining which has also resulted in the harassment of the indigenous peoples (IPs) living in the area.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,p.47)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2016-09-06

rows.author: I104;
rows.title_full: SAD PLIGHT OF OFWs
rows.title_short: King Saud's Directive For Foreign Workers
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bertiz rose to relate the confirmation of the
royal directives issued by His Majesty King Salman
bin Abdulaziz al Saud of the Kingdom of Saudi
Arabia regarding the protection of the rights of
foreign workers, including the 11,000 overseas
Filipino workers (OFWs) based at Saudi Oger and
other similarly situated companies. He stressed that the problems of the OFWs did not happen overnight, and underscored how the present Administration has quickly and concretely acted on their situation. After mentioning that he filed House Resolution No. 13 urging the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) and the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) to help the stranded OFWs in Saudi Arabia, Rep. Bertiz disclosed that the ACTS-OFW Party-List has also initiated a dialogue between the families of said workers and various government agencies to identify the government programs involved. He said that he would join the
government´s crisis team to Saudi Arabia, being the lone Representative of the OFW sector in the House of Representatives. Finally, as a former OFW who has also experienced the hardships and sacrifices of stranded overseas workers, he sought for the approval of House Resolution No. 157 thanking King Salman of Saudi Arabia for his act of benevolence and compassion, and also honoring and thanking President Duterte for mobilizing government resources to address the problem.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BELARO
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep.
Tugna, Rep. Salvador B. Belaro Jr. inquired why the problems of the OFWs in Saudi Arabia were resolved through foreign intervention and not by the national government. He also inquired into the role of the DOLE and the DFA on the issue. He lamented the deplorable handling of the situation of the OFWs, and suggested the filing of a resolution investigating the government officials concerned. Agreeing therewith, Rep. Bertiz said that the Office of the Undersecretary for Migrant Workers´ Affairs in particular should be investigated. He sought support for House Resolution No. 194 which he authored seeking for the creation of the Department of Migration and Development to address the exclusive needs of the OFWs. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,p.47)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2016-09-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Delaro

rows.author: I036;
rows.title_short: Olympic Silver Medal Of Hidlyn Diaz
rows.abstract:
Rep. Lopez (M.) took the floor to give due honor
and recognition to Ms. Hidilyn Diaz for bagging the silver medal in the 53-kilogram class in the women´s division weightlifting competition at the 31st Olympiad currently being held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. After informing his peers of his personal knowledge of Ms. Diaz´s struggles as an athlete from the first time she joined the weightlifting competition until her victory at the Rio Olympics, Rep. Lopez said that in recognition of a well-deserved victory, he and other Members have filed House Resolutions commending and congratulating Ms. Diaz and the Philippine Weightlifting Association headed by former Rep. Monico O. Puentevella for bringing pride and honor to the country. Moreover, he said that he would take the cudgels in ensuring that the interest of the national athletes will have a voice in the House. He also commended the Filipino sportsmen and sportswomen who embody the hopes and aspirations of the people for their dedication and
outstanding representation of the nation. In closing, he expressed hope that the nation would take inspiration from the athletes who have
demonstrated what teamwork and unity can achieve
and that the example of Olympians would continue to be a source of positive transformation in the life journey of the nation and the people. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,p.48)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-08-09
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Lobregat, Dalipe, Del Rosario, Bordado and Zubiri.

rows.author: G003;
rows.title_full: IMPORTANCE OF AND MISCONCEPTIONS ABOUT BREASTFEEDING
rows.abstract:
Rep. Aglipay-Villar talked about the importance
of and misconceptions about breastfeeding as she
noted that August is being celebrated as the National Breastfeeding Month and the previous week was World Breastfeeding Week. Citing her personal experiences as a breastfeeding mother, she explained how breastfeeding was a personal choice but was not a moral issue nor an issue only about women; and cited the lack of facilities for and public knowledge and awareness about breastfeeding. After presenting studies and facts and figures, she stressed that breastfeeding
is a public health issue of national significance
that would address not only malnutrition, disease,
and mortality in the women´s and children´s
sectors but hunger, poverty, and economic growth
and equality in the country and society as a whole. The Lady Legislator then asked the Members to prioritize bills that she had filed on infant feeding, a maternal health program, and a 100-day maternity leave; and to promote breastfeeding through various modes of media. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.8,p.28)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2016-08-09
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Cayetano, Antonino, Herrera-Dy, Biazon, Almario and De Jesus. Remarks of Rep.Kho.

rows.author: I081;
rows.title_full: NEED TO PASS HOUSE BILL NO.56, RAISING THE SALARIES OF PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, GOVERMENT EMPLOYEES AND INSTRUCTORS OF STATE COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. France L. Castro,
speaking in Filipino, said that she was glad and
could not believe that she would become a Member
of the House of Representatives as a teacher representing the Act Teachers Party-List. Being a product of public school whose dream was to change the country´s system of education, she then narrated how her parents who did not finish even elementary education had prioritized their children´s education. Rep. Castro said that she was proud to be an active member of the Alliance of Concerned Teachers since 1989, one of the board of directors of the Philippine Public School Teachers, and at present, a member of the World Executive Board of Education International.
Thereafter, Rep. Castro lamented on the experiences that she had to go through when she was still a public school teacher, and as a former president of the Quezon City Public School Teachers´ Association. For this reason, she sought her colleagues´ support for House Bill No. 56, raising the salaries of public school teachers, government employees and instructors of State colleges and universities. Lastly, she made the call for a salary increase and income tax reduction.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.8,p.30)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2016-09-06

rows.abstract:
Rep. Lagman cited 12 major reasons which render
the late President Ferdinand E. Marcos unfit to be
buried in the Libingan ng mga Bayani . . . Rep. Lagman pointed out that the then pervasive
nonchalance of most Filipinos to the homecoming of
Marcos´ remains has today been supplanted by a
growing opposition to the proposed Marcos burial at the Heroes´ Cemetery or the Libingan ng mga Bayani. He stated that among those opposed to the plan are the human rights advocates and families of victims of human rights violations during martial law. Considering that President Rodrigo Roa Duterte´s predisposition to bury the late President Marcos in the Libingan ng mga Bayani is a gross departure from his previous statement during his SONA, Rep. Lagman said that the interment of Marcos´ remains in the Libingan ng mga Bayani is an undeserved reward and it is not a day of reckoning. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.8,pp.23-24)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-08-09
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Villarin, Manifestation by Rep. Atienza.

rows.author: I090;
rows.abstract:
In commemoration of the International Humanitarian
Law (IHL) Day, Rep. Roque spoke on the significance of the IHL which seeks to protect individuals and civilians who are not actively taking part in any armed conflict. He stated that the country has made strides in strengthening its commitment and adherence to the IHL by adopting laws such as Republic Act (RA) No. 9851 or the Philippine Act on Crimes Against International Humanitarian Law, Genocide, and Other Crimes Against Humanity, as well as ratifying conventions such as the 1948 Genocide Convention and its Additional Protocols. He pointed out however that the culture of impunity in the country and the serious violations on the IHL still continue especially on the impact of conflict to children and indigenous communities and the rise in the number of displaced persons due to conflict and
violence. In this regard, Rep. Roque said that he will file a proposed IHL Amendatory Act which seeks to address infirmities in RA No. 9851, as well as a proposed Philippine-ICC Cooperation Act aimed at facilitating compliance with the Philippines´ obligations under the Rome Statute. As he stated that these bills were an output
of the Technical Working Group (TWG) of the
ICC Implementation Project of the Institute of International Legal Studies of the U.P. Law Center, he thanked the members and experts of the TWG composed of the Institute of International Legal Studies UP Law Center, the UP College of Law; other government agencies; nongovernmental organizations and civil society groups. While Rep. Roque urged the Members to do their part in the fight against heinous crimes and to ensure
sanctions against the most horrendous violations that can be committed in times of armed conflict, he also pointed out that it is in their power to help uphold the rule of law in the country and the system of international justice. He then greeted everyone a happy IHL Day. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.9,p.29)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2016-09-06

rows.author: I062;
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Edgar Mary S. Sarmiento from the First District of Samar, spoke on a proposal to ease Metro Manila´s traffic situation by adopting the one-way traffic system used in New York City, among others. He explained in detail how the three major road arteries in Metro Manila can serve as a one-way interstate highway by allowing exit to the different communities with the same traffic flow and
doubling the road capacity so that the proposed bus rapid transit system (BRT) can be introduced at the soonest possible time. He added that the BRT will eliminate the problem of undisciplined bus drivers and that the bus companies will become the owner of a consortium firm that they will be forming. Furthermore, for the efficient movement of passengers and goods to attain a higher productivity level, Rep. Sarmiento recommended that: 1) provincial buses should no longer be allowed in EDSA; 2) the LRT and MRT terminals´ loading and unloading areas should also serve as the only loading and unloading terminals for the buses; and 3) delivery trucks will only be allowed on the outermost lanes provided they will still follow the scheduled truck ban. The solution to traffic, Rep. Sarmiento (E.) said, would be a legislative proposal to grant emergency
powers to the President. He expressed belief that the traffic situation calls for every doable and practical solution possible. INTERPELLATION OF REP. DE VENECIA. On Rep. De Venecia´s query, Rep. Sarmiento stated that much as he wanted to introduce the Pasig River ferry system, it is not sustainable because most passengers would rather ride the railway system than the ferry. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.29-30)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-08-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. De Venecia

rows.author: I083;
rows.abstract:
Elago said that they are one with the youth of the
world in celebrating the International Youth Day on Friday, August 12, 2016. Rep. Elago thereafter delved on 1) the needs and demands of the youth and the student sector; 2) the problems besetting students, including the deregulation and privatization of education; 3) the forced enrollment to private senior high schools
due to the insufficiency of public senior high school facilities; 4) the crisis in the country´s public tertiary education system; and 5) the implementation of antistudent policies which become forms of repression and democratic rights violations, among others. Finally, Rep. Elago stressed that there is no better way to celebrate the International Youth Day than to reignite the commitment of the youth to fulfill their
historical role to side with the oppressed and the marginalized, and to fight for freedom and civil liberties of the Filipino people. INTERPELLATION OF REP. BORDADO Rep. Bordado sought clarification on his colleague´s advocacy and said that while he agreed therewith, the problem was that history books contained inaccuracies and errors. Rep. Elago explained that the Kabataan Party-List was fighting for a nationalistic, scientific, and massoriented education system. She added that nationalism meant teaching history from the perspective of the Filipino people and promoting awareness of the fact that many Filipino heroes were very young. She stressed that history books, especially textbooks, should be reviewed and corrected. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.9,p.30)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-08-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Bordado

rows.author: I066;
rows.title_full: ILLEGAL MINING IN NEGROS ORIENTAL
rows.abstract:
While at the same time presenting a slideshow
presentation about his topic, Rep. Teves spoke about an ongoing quarrying operation in his province, and sought clarification who between the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Secretary Gina Lopez and the incumbent provincial governor has jurisdiction over the matter and should be made answerable to the people; whether the operation should be considered as small or large scale quarrying/mining; and whether the provincial governor should be sanctioned for granting a permit to operate even in the absence of benching. He expressed hope
that the Duterte Administration would act on the matter at the soonest possible time.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. LIMKAICHONG. Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Jocelyn Sy Limkaichong at the outset said that she shares the sentiments of Rep. Teves considering that she is also from the province of Negros Oriental. On successive queries of Rep. Limkaichong, Rep. Teves said that the pictures he had presented would already speak for themselves. He also requested the DENR to check whether the export and recorded volumes were properly recorded by the mining company. He disclosed that years back, the DENR had said that
it was not under their jurisdiction but it was the prerogative of the governor to issue mining permits. Considering that Rep. Teves has no data to substantiate his claim, Rep. Limkaichong moved that the latter´s verbatim speech and its accompanying pictures be forwarded to DENR Secretary Lopez for further investigation.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.10,pp.20-21)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2016-09-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Limkaichong

rows.author: I030;
rows.title_full: MEASURES TO SOLVE THE PROBLEM OF LABOR CONTRACTING
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Mark O. Go from
the Lone District of Baguio City dealt with the issue of contractualization or the contracting out of work to independent contractors as against the prohibited labor-only contracting; the real situation of the ordinary Filipino workers; the difference between illegal and legal service contractors; the attempts in past Congresses
to amend the pertinent provisions of the Labor
Code on labor contracting and security of tenure of workers; and the current business and economic trends which tend to promote labor-only contracting but which should never jeopardize the rights, welfare and lives of Filipino workers.
He then cited the following requirements and conditions that must be complied with if job contracting or outsourcing is to be allowed in the country; 1) not more than 10 to 20 percent of the total employees shall be contractual employees; 2) no employee should be terminated without just cause and due process as provided for in the Labor Code, within the period of his contract; 3) the right to self-organization shall be guaranteed;
4) provision for skill development and training
must be established; and 5) the company engaged in
outsourcing must be registered with the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE). Finally, he urged his colleagues to support his proposed bill amending the Labor Code to arrive at a win-win situation both for the employees and employers. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.10,p.21)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2016-09-06

rows.author: I010;
rows.title_full: THE LATE SECRETARY ROBREDO, GOOD GOVERNANCE AND PEOPLE PARTICIPATION
rows.abstract:
Initially, Rep. Bordado thanked President Rodrigo
Roa Duterte for declaring August 18, 2016 as a special nonworking day in Naga City to commemorate the 4th death anniversary of former City Mayor and Secretary of the Interior and Local Government Jesse M. Robredo. Rep. Bordado pointed out that Mayor Jesse Manalastas Robredo, the first Philippine mayor who had been conferred the prestigious Ramon Magsaysay Award (the Asian counterpart of the Nobel Prize), transformed Naga City and laid the groundwork for people´s participation therein. He said that the latter
formulated the Good Governance Model which consisted of a progressive perspective, functional partnerships, and people´s participation; prioritized growth with equity; and established and encouraged partnerships with various public and private sectors. In summing up his speech, Rep. Bordado held that Mayor Robredo´s legacy of people´s participation in local governance was secure not only in his city but in the entire country; and remarked that the mayor did not even have to be buried in the Libingan ng Mga Bayani. MANIFESTATION OF REP. BELARO
On behalf of his fellow-educators and fellow-Bicolanos, Rep. Belaro congratulated Rep. Bordado for his passionate and timely speech on Mayor Robredo whom he called a genuine hero.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.10,pp.21-22)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2016-09-06
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep. Belaro

rows.title_full: WITHDRAWAL OF CEBU CITY MAYOR TOMMY OSMENA'S DEPUTATION AS A REPRESENTATIVE OF THE NATIONAL POLICE COMMISSION (NAPOLCOM)
rows.abstract:
On further motion of Rep. Bondoc, there being no
objection, the Chair recognized Rep. Raul V. Del Mar from the First District of Cebu City who questioned the withdrawal of Cebu City Mayor Tommy Osmeña´s deputation as a representative of the National Police Commission (Napolcom). After adverting to Republic Act No. 8551 which provides for the automatic deputation of governors and mayors as Napolcom agents and the grounds for the withdrawal of the same, he cited Napolcom Resolution No. 2016-467 enumerating Mayor Osmeña´s actions that were considered inimical to national security and the President´s peace and order campaign. He thereafter relayed one by one the City of Cebu´s refuting the allegations,
initially stating that what was stopped was not
the police officers´ allowances but their cash rewards that came from the mayor´s personal funds.
As he clarified Cebu City´s budgetary support to
the local police units, Rep. Del Mar stated that the Napolcom was grossly misinformed that Cebu City Mayor Osmeña was guilty of engaging in acts inimical to national security or which negate the effectiveness of the peace and order campaign. He also stated that neither he nor Rep. Rodrigo A. Abellanosa of the Second District of Cebu City was consulted by the Napolcom with regard to the withdrawal of Mayor Osmeña´s deputation. As such, he requested the House Committee on Local Government to investigate the legality and propriety of the Napolcom´s withdrawal of deputation of Mayor Osmeña. INTERPELLATION
OF REP. ABELLANOSA Reps. Abellanosa and Del Mar discussed the matter of the reward money given by Cebu City Mayor Osmeña and the pullout of his police escorts. They also delved into Cebu City´s budgetary support to the local police units which may have been the reason for the Napolcom´s resolution withdrawing Mayor Osmeña´s deputation as his actions were considered inimical to national security and the govenrment´s peace and order campaign. INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Reps. Atienza and Del Mar exchanged views on
the Napolcom´s stripping of Cebu City Mayor Osmeña´s police control; agreed that the principle of local autonomy allowing police control is enshrined in the Constitution and vital in the achievement of peace and order as now being pursued by President Duterte; supported Rep. Del Mar´s call for a congressional inquiry into the Napolcom as well as a review of the PNP Law; and expressed support to Mayor Osmena´s fight for his right to police control. Rep. Atienza then congratulated and reiterated his support to Rep. Del Mar and urged Congress to adhere to the intentions of the Constitution by respecting the
autonomy of the LGUs in allowing mayors full control and supervision of their local police force.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.10,pp.22-23)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2016-09-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Abellanos and Atienza

rows.author: I070;
rows.title_full: COMPLAINED ON THE PEACE AND ORDER SITUATION IN THE 3RD DISTRICT OF NUEVA ECIJA
rows.title_short: Corruption In Relation To Her Disqualification Case
rows.abstract:
Rep. Vergara initially said that corruption, which
she defined as abuse of power for private gain, was pervasive, systemic, and prevalent in the country. She then said that because of countless instances of shooting and murder of barangay officials in her district and the inaction thereon by Nueva Ecija Governor Aurelio Umali and his wife, Representative Cherry Umali, she ran under the platform of change and progress against the influential and well connected couple who used to be a political ally and ruled over the province for the last 15 years. She stressed that she wanted to protect the weakest members of the political chain and will file and support measures that will entitle barangay officials to insurance coverage and pension under the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS). She subsequently alleged that several officials of the Bureau of Immigration, whom she named, had conspired and tampered with official government documents to support several disqualification cases filed against her in order to benefit the Umalis and help them remain in power. She stressed that Congress must pass a law providing more severe punishment for corrupt public servants. She maintained that the country must be ruled by laws and not connections and must treat all Filipinos with equal respect and courtesy regardless of social, economic, and educational stature. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.11,pp.14-15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2016-09-06

rows.author: I101;
rows.title_full: IMPROPER IMPLEMENTATION OF THE EMISSION TESTING PROVISION OF THE PHILIPPINE CLEAN AIR ACT OF 1999
rows.abstract:
Rep. Abayon spoke on the issue of the improper
implementation of the emission testing provision of the Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999. He relayed the concern of one of his constituents regarding emission testing and inquired into the status of emission testing centers as he lamented that there are certain unscrupulous individuals who are taking advantage of the situation for their personal gain. As such, he urged the Departments of Trade and Industry (DTI), and
Transportation (DOTr) to review the accreditation of the authorized emission testing centers.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SANDOVAL
Rep. Sandoval agreed with the concerns raised by
Rep. Abayon and likewise disclosed that fake
apprehending officers who are not connected with the Land Transportation Office (LTO) are rampant along Epifanio delos Santos Avenue (EDSA) and prey on unsuspecting motorists. They also dwelled on the issue of unscrupulous emission testing operators who allow emission testing of vehicles in absentia but are still given permits to operate by the LTO; the endless approval of permits to operate private emission testing centers; and the need for the LTO and the DOTr to review the system of emission testing. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.11,pp.17&18)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2016-09-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Sandoval

rows.author: I088;
rows.title_full: SAD STATE OF INTERNET ACCESS IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Gullas, Rep. Enrico A. Pineda from 1-PACMAN Party-List first emphasized the important role as well as the social and economic impact of telecommunications throughout the world, this as he noted that reliable networks could be found in top
industrialized nations while developing countries are still working diligently to attain this level.
As he observed that the Philippines has been
lagging behind in terms of internet connectivity and cellular services that it has already been outranked by its neighboring countries, he lamented that the Filipinos also suffer from costly broadband and internet charges. He thereafter emphasized the National Telecommunications Commission´s (NTC) task of reviewing and safeguarding the operations of
the telecom industry, particularly in the light of
President Rodrigo R. Duterte´s warning to
telecommunications companies (Telcos) “to shape up
or face the consequences.” He concluded that the
Filipinos deserve better services which, he hoped,
would be provided by the telcos.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.11,p.18)
rows.status: Scheduled for meeting/hearing on 2016-11-16
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Belaro, Sy-Alvarado and Teves

rows.author: G110;
rows.title_full: DRUG REHABILITATION WOULD BE BETTER ADDRESSED BY A COMPREHENSIVE AND SUSTAINABLE PLAN THAT AIMS TO ESTABLISH ADDITIONAL DRUG REHABILITATION CENTERS STRATEGICALLY LOCATED IN EACH LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT OF THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract:
Rep. Batocabe delved on the recent development
on the war against drugs and what to do with the mass surrenderees. He averred that the drug rehabilitation issue would be better addressed by a comprehensive and sustainable plan that aims to establish additional drug rehabilitation centers strategically located in each legislative district of the country. As he cited more statistics, Rep. Batocabe said that what the government needs is to appropriate around P33 billion for the drug rehabilitation program as he remarked that it had allocated more than that amount for the Conditional Cash Transfer Program. He then
proposed to increase admissions in existing
rehabilitation centers; build additional centers or at least one center in each district; and consider the temporary use of military camps and government hospitals to treat drug dependents. He thereafter urged for a comprehensive and long-term plan on how to address the rehabilitation of the drug dependents and that the war against drugs should include saving lives and protecting the welfare and rights of the people. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.11,pp.18-19)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on DANGEROUS DRUGS since 2016-09-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Biazon and Tugna

rows.author: I020;
rows.title_full: NEED FOR A MULTI-SECTORAL APPROACH ON THE GOVERNMENT'S CAMPAIGN AGAINST ILLEGAL DRUGS
rows.abstract:
Initially, Rep. De Venecia expressed support for
the President´s war against drugs and decried the killing by a vigilante squad of one of his constituents who was mistaken to be a drug pusher. He then stressed that while the Philippine National Police (PNP) continues to identify, apprehend and fight drug users/pushers, the government should adopt a multisectoral and preventive policy on the drug problem which includes the following: 1) enactment of laws and mechanisms to reduce the supply and demand of drugs; 2) convening, funding and monitoring of barangay antidrug abuse councils (BADACs); 3) inclusion of drug education in the education curriculum; 4) establishment and expansion of drug rehabilitation centers, programs, facilities,
personnel and funds; and the temporary use of
military camps as rehabilitation centers; 5) media collaboration on drug awareness; and 6) social reintegration and livelihood programs for rehabilitated dependents. As he called on the Department of Health (DOH), media conglomerates, mass media, and the Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB), among others, to work hand-in-hand in the propagation of drug prevention measures and mechanisms, Rep. De Venecia stated that the multisectoral approach to the war on drugs under President Rodrigo
Roa Duterte´s leadership could set a model for the
whole world, one that is not isolationist and exclusive but collaborative and inclusive. He stressed that to ensure the success of such an approach, different government agencies such as the National Youth Commission (NYC), Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA), among others, should also provide support mechanisms in order for the war on drugs to succeed. Thereupon, Rep. De Venecia 1) enjoined his colleagues to support the passage of the Bills he would file, 2) called on the Appropriations and Health committees
of Congress to increase the national health
budget that would expand and modernize existing rehabilitation centers in the country, and 3) emphasized the improvement and effective implementation of drug assessment and monitoring programs in the barangay and regional health centers. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.12,pp.22-23)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on DANGEROUS DRUGS since 2016-08-17
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Maceda, Tugna, Atienza, Herrera-Dy, Roman, Bolilia, Vergara, Cayetano, Andaya and Biazon

rows.author: G105;
rows.title_full: INEFFICIENCY OF INTERNET SERVICE PROVIDERS
rows.abstract:
As Rep. De Jesus assailed in Filipino the poor
cellphone services as well as the penalties and hidden fees charged by telecommunications companies (telcos) to the consumers, she related her personal experience of customer service troubles as a postpaid subscriber who had used the same cellphone number in the last 13 years and had recently applied for an upgrade of her postpaid plan. She recalled the difficulties she encountered because 1) she had to wait long as her transaction had to pass through customer service representatives in a call center; 2) she was charged for a decade-long bill that was never reflected in her statement of account so she
was forced to stop the subscription for the particular cellphone number; 3) her application for a new postpaid plan was cut because she was told that she had to settle first her old account; 4) she suffered from a daylong disconnection that she had to personally talk to the OIC manager and put in writing her complaint. . .
House Journal No.13,p.11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY since 2016-09-06

rows.author: I036;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Manuel Luis T. Lopez...spoke on two important events in Philippine history that happened in August 21: 1) the Plaza Miranda bombing during the miting de avance of the opposition Liberal Party; and 2) when Ninoy Aquino upon his return home after a three-year exile in the United States was gunned down at the tarmac of the old Manila International Airport... cited the important lessons that the people should learn from these two important events and expressed hope that the young would look back and reflect on the lessons learned on this very significant day and recall the sacrifice and heroism of these brave and

Rep. Atienza... stood up to speak on the same
event on August 21, 1971 wherein he, gladly stood up in front of the people in Plaza Miranda

rows.author: I056;
rows.title_full: WATER PROBLEM IN SAN JOSE DEL MONTE
rows.abstract:
Rep. Robes delved into the current water crisis affecting her Lone District in Bulacan which has been waterless for the past six days. She then commented on the ineptitude of the city´s local water district in addressing the problem. She said that the San Jose Del Monte City Water District´s (SJDMCWD) plan to resort to borrowings will only result in the increase of the very high water
charges that her constituents were already suffering from despite inefficient water services. As she complained about the SJDMCWD´s lack of social responsibility, she discussed the contributory factors to the water crisis...
Thereupon, Rep. Robes asked the national government to allow more private concessionaires to enter San Jose Del Monte City and to enact legislations to check the operations of local water districts... (House Journal No.13,p.13)

rows.author: I066;
rows.title_full: LOCAL EXECUTIVE POWER OVER THE POLICE
rows.title_short: Alleged Harassment Of Phil. National Police Director Against Him
rows.abstract:
Alleging that the governor of Negros Oriental had
been using the provincial police director to harass his political opponents, Rep. Teves said that the former relieved several police chiefs for no reason at all and without offering the mayors concerned with several replacements for the same and planned to implicate him with possession of illegal drugs and firearms in his residence. He also alleged that the governor was using said police director to operate his money-making
schemes...; called for an investigation into the illegal activities in his province and requested
PNP Regional Dir.Conrad Capa to immediately relieve police Provincial Dir. Nestor Tiempo from his post as the mandate of the police is to protect the people and not to be a partisan to a provincial governor. (House Journal No.13,p.13)

rows.author: H045;
rows.title_full: COMMUNITY-BASED PROGRAMS HE HAS INITIATED IN HIS DISTRICT TO COUNTER THE THREAT OF ILLEGAL DRUGS
rows.abstract:
Rep. Oaminal spoke on the threat of illegal drugs
which is among the greatest evils that the country
faces and threatens to eat away at the very foundation it is built upon...; informed the Body of some of the community-based programs and seminars he had initiated ... In the aftermath of President Duterte´s announcement, he continued, some of the leaders and people in the province reported to him the insinuations made by the camp of Mayor Reynaldo “Aldong” Parojinog Sr. of Ozamiz City that Rep. Oaminal was responsible for making a report to the President that led to the inclusion of their names in the list and that the said mayor and company have retaliated by using their connections and resources to come up with dossiers that would connect Rep. Oaminal to illegal drugs. He thereafter denied said insinuations and expressed confidence that should the authorities receive such dossiers, they will properly validate and investigate any outrageous claims...; expressed support to Rep. Rodel M. Batocabe´s call in his privilege speech ... for the inclusion in the 2017 national budget of a program to rehabilitate drug addicts, and called on his colleagues to support the President´s fight against illegal drugs.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.13,p.14)

rows.title_full: NEED TO PASS A COMPREHENSIVE AGRARIAN REFORM LAW ACHIEVE PEACE AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THE COUNTRYSIDE
rows.abstract:
Rep. Villarin spoke on the issue of agrarian reform, specifically discussing the implementation of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Law (CARL)
which he said, the government must address in order to achieve peace and sustainable development in the countryside. He pointed out that President Rodrigo Roa Duterte made an emphatic commitment to agrarian reform when he appointed a genuine peasant leader and a true champion of the farmers, Rafael “Ka Paeng” V. Mariano as Secretary of Agrarian Reform...; made a narrative summary of the implementation of the CARL as well as the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program Extension with Reforms (CARPER) Act under Republic Act 9700 during the past administrations,...
(SOURCE: House Journal No.14,p.15)

rows.author: I066;
rows.title_full: MANDATE OF HOSPITALS TO SAVE LIVES
rows.abstract:
Rep. Teves´ privilege speech is a reminder to all
hospitals ... that their priority mandate is to save lives and not to make profit. He gave this reminder in light of what just happened to one of his constituents who asked for his help in securing blood for her child who was down with dengue. He said that it was just fortunate that he was able to talk to a former classmate who was an officer at the Siliman University Medical Center so they were able to obtain blood bags ... which the blood donors used and bring the blood to the Negros Oriental Provincial Hospital ... Rep. Teves was told earlier by Rep. Raul V. Del Mar that there was already a law prohibiting hospitals from not admitting patients without initial payment...
(SOURCE: House Journal No.15,p.20)
