rows.author: I010;
rows.title_full: A NATIONAL BUDGET RESPONSIVE TO NEEDS OF THE PEOPLE
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bordado discussed the importance of the national budget especially the budgetary
allocation to the different government agencies for the delivery of basic services to the people;  stressed that ..., there is a need to examine
the absorptive capacities of all departments, assess the regional allocation of public investments, and review whether the allocation of resources has been done in a manner that no department or agency receives more resources at the expense of another; expressed concern on the budgetary cuts in the 2017 proposed budgets of the Departments of Health (DOH), and Agriculture (DA) ...; affirmed that the government must vigorously pursue the strategy of allocating resources to local government units (LGUs)...; urged Congress to ... to immediately craft the Budget Reform Act with the assistance of the Department of Budget and Management (DBM). INTERPELLATION OF REP. ANDAYA  With respect to the President´s promise of doubling the salaries of policemen, soldiers, teachers and other members of the civil bureaucracy, Rep. Andaya said that this would cost the government some P230 billion, and asked where this amount of money would be sourced... INTERPELLATION OF REP. MARCOLETA
Rep. Rodante D. Marcoleta ... noted that Rep. Bordado cited several areas where poverty incidence rate is so wide as compared to other areas, like the case of Central Luzon with a
poverty incidence rate of 11 to 12 percent, as compared to Mindanao, particularly the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM) with a rate of
more than 50 percent. He said that the wide inequity in the country is represented by the so-called per capita income, which is arrived at by dividing the gross domestic product (GDP) with the total population. He cited the case of the ARMM with a per capita income of about P11,000, as compared to that of the National Capital Region´s P219,000.00...(SOURCE: House Jornal No.15,pp.21-22)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2016-09-14
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Andaya and Marcoleta

rows.author: C045;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Farinas said that several questions had been raised re: the position of Minority Leader days after the opening of the 1st Regular Session of the 17th Congress ..., and that the point of contention now is whether the House should follow tradition or the Rules of the House. He noted that the Members who are invoking that Rep. Teddy Brawner Baguilat Jr. is the duly elected Minority Leader claim to have tradition and customs and usage on their part. He then focused his speech on the basis of their claim. For the guidance of all concerned and future Congresses, he said that he would like to present before the Body how the selection or election of Minority Leader has evolved and proceeded to show a matrix of how in the 13th Congress this election has evolved,
when it was specifically stated in Section 7 of the Rules of the House how the Majority Leader and Minority Leaders are elected... He expressed hope that he has explained clearly what happened that the 17th Congress only adopted the rule as clearly stated in the House Rules. Inasmuch as the Philippines is a Republican government where sovereignty resides in the people and all government authority emanates from them, he said that no one can hold public office if the people do not give him their mandate, be it a Minority Leader, because one cannot be a Minority Leader by default or by losing. (SOURCE: House Journal No.15,pp.32-34)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-08-24

rows.title_full: DISAPPEARED HEROES AND MARTYRS AND THE CONVENTION ON ENFORCED DISAPPEARANCE
rows.abstract:
Rep. Lagman ... privilege speech, entitled, “Disappeared Heroes and Martyrs” in celebration of the United Nations International Day of the Disappeared, to wit:
Mr. Speaker, esteemed colleagues:
Five years ago, the United Nations declared August 30 as International Day of the Disappeared.
Today, as we pay tribute to the desaparecidos, we recognize their inspiring feats as heroes and martyrs of freedom and democracy. Today, we demand justice for all victims of enforced disappearance and their families in no less than 88 countries
including the Philippines. The desaparecidos were abducted by agents of the State or by persons acting with their support or acquiescence,
but who refuse to disclose any information on their custody or whereabouts. Their inquiries being stonewalled, the families remain clueless about their disappeared loved ones´ fate - many up
to this very day ... there are 2,239 reported victims of enforced disappearance from 1971 to the present administration. The unreported could be much higher. The Marcos regime registered the biggest number of reported victims of which 856 have been documented by the Families of Victims of Involuntary Disappearance (FIND), a human rights organization established at the height of the people´s resistance to the Marcos dictatorship ...Under the current administration, however, there are roadblocks to their full recovery and reintegration into the mainstream of society. These include the brazen commission of extrajudicial killings of suspected drug dependents, drug pushers, and other criminals. The violent drug-and crime-busting inevitably reminds them of the harrowing fate of their disappeared kin. In the same vein, the proposed burial of the remains of the chief violator of human rights during martial law in the Libingan ng mga Bayani opens old wounds that have not really healed in the absence of closure as justice remains elusive.
Today as we mark the International Day of the Disappeared, I join the families of desaparecidos in urging Congress to exercise its oversight function to ensure that R.A. 10353 is fully and strictly implemented. (SOURCE: House Journal No.16,pp.23-25)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2016-09-14
rows.remarks: For inclusion into the Records

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: FORMULATION OF A NATIONAL SECURITY POLICY AND STRATEGY
rows.title_short: Armed Forces Of The Filipino People
rows.abstract:
In observance of the Armed Forces of the Filipino
People Week (AFFPW) mandated under R.A.No.10664, Rep. Alejano spoke on the extraordinary services of the men and women of the armed forces who have relentlessly served the country and continue to fulfill their mandate as the protector of the
people and the State, and secure its sovereignty and the integrity of its national territory...; lamented however that in spite of the AFP Modernization Program, the AFP remained wanting in materials and equipment which has resulted in the death of an estimated 2,000 soldiers during the past ten years and a number of them wounded but psychologically scarred and traumatized. As such,
he enjoined his colleagues to formulate a National Security Policy and Strategy aimed at achieving national security objectives with the available resources and making sure that the programs and projects of the DND are in line with the stated capabilities of the military that need to be developed...; referred to the hearing conducted by the Cttee. on Veterans Affairs in the last Congress, where it was found out that the money remitted to the board of trustees of WWII veterans by the PVB was not sufficient and that the national government has no authority over the bank because it is governed by its own charter...; explained in detail the general office uniform of the Phil. Marine Corps which he joined as a memeber of the reserved unit...; discussed his position on the ongoing peace talks between the government and the CPP-NPA-NDF...(SOURCE: House Journal No.16,p.25)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2016-09-14
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Belaro and Daza

rows.author: H029;
rows.title_full: MISMANAGEMENT OF THE CEBU PROVINCIAL DETENTION AND REHABILITATION CENTER
rows.abstract:
...Rep. Garcia first related how the Cebu Provincial Detention and Rehabilitation Center (CPDRC) was transformed into a world-renowned and world-class facility and became a source of pride, inspiration, and hope for rehabilitation and redemption of inmates thereof and for the country in general during her nineyear term as Cebu governor.  Subsequently, she lamented how it disintegrated since Governor Hilario Davide III assumed office in 2013 and recounted the
recent raids that yielded millions in cash money, 
illegal drugs, gadgets and appliances, weapons, and drug paraphernalia among the inmates and jail guards within and outside of the center´s premises...;stressed that Governor Davide must be made to answer the issues and not skirt the matter by suggesting the transfer of the CPDRC management to the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology 
(BJMP). She reminded Governor Davide that as the 
provincial governor, he is the keeper of the provincial jail as provided for in Section 1731, Article III of the Revised Administrative Code of 1917 and Section 468, Article III of the 1991 Local Government Code (LGC)...;informed the Body that she would file a resolution calling for an investigation, in aid of legislation, into the glaring deficiencies and gross mismanagement and administration of the CPDRC. (SOURCE: House Journal No.17,pp.18-22)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2016-09-14
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Salimbangon and Teves

rows.author: I010;
rows.title_full: NEED FOR AN EFFICIENT SYSTEM TO IMPLEMENT THE PROTECTIVE SERVICES PROGRAM (PSP) OF THE DSWD
rows.title_short: Commission On Audit / Department Of Social Welfare And Development Circular
rows.abstract:
... Rep. Gabriel H. Bordado Jr...spoke about MC No. 9 issued by the DSWD Secretary, entitled, “Supplemental Guidelines on the Implementation of the Protective Services Program (PSP),” in relation to the Supreme Court decision declaring the unconstitutionality of the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF).  He 
said that the DSWD Circular underscores, among others, that “referral letters from individuals, group of individuals or organizations including public officials ... are not integral to the implementation of the PSP and that the DSWD retains the sole authority to determine the beneficiaries of the program pursuant to existing guidelines.”...; pointed out that there should be an effective and efficient system to ensure that qualified beneficiaries will have proper access to the program, and that an intensive information dissemination campaign is set up...; reminded the DSWD Secretary of President Duterte´s vow to end the long queues for those who wish to avail 
themselves of government services.(SOURCE: House Journal No.17,p.22)

rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Andaya

rows.author: G064;
rows.title_full: NEED TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPABILITIES OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO FIGHT TERRORISM AND LAWLESSNESS IN THE LIGHT OF THE DAVAO CITY BOMBING
rows.title_short: Night Market Bombing In Davao City
rows.abstract:
Rep. Nograles spoke on the Davao City bombing 
last September 2, 2016 which killed 14 innocent civilians and seriously wounded 67 others...; stressed that they cannot live in fear and made 
a challenge to let their fears be swept away by the strength of their collective moral outrage and fortify their resolve, as individual citizens and as a nation, to fight against all forms of lawlessness, criminality and terrorism...; noted that the President, who is a true son of Davao, has issued the strongest call to arms against 
lawlessness in the wake of said bombing by declaring a state of lawless violence and for such purpose, has mobilized the full force of the armed forces and the police, and has been exhorting the citizenry to take part in the war against criminality and lawlessness...; stated that he filed House Resolution No. 302 condemning the bombing of the Roxas Night Market in Davao City, and expressing the resolve of the House to undertake appropriate actions to strengthen the capabilities of local communities to fight terrorism and lawlessness,...(SOURCE: House Journal No.18,p.11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2016-09-14
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Roque H., Atienza, Alejano, Lobrega and Dimaporo M.; Manifestations by Reps. Hernandez F.and Zarate.

rows.author: I096;
rows.title_full: NEED TO ADDRESS THE CONCERN OF MILLIONS OF INFORMAL SETTLERS IN HIGHLY URBANIZED PARTS OF THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract:
...Rep. Villarin...spoke on the challenge of addressing the concern of millions of informal settlers in Metro Manila, as well as in other highly urbanized parts of the country...; mentioned several problems related to urbanization and informal settlements, including among others, the increase in the number of informal settlers in recent years, the supposed housing backlog for informal settler families, and the ineffectiveness of the national government´s effort in focusing on off-city housing projects. As Vice President Leni Robredo has declared the suspension of off-city resettlement programs while President Duterte has announced a “no eviction, no demolition without resettlement” policy, Rep. Villarin asked where the government would get the funds if they would focus on in-city housing projects considering that the NHA funds have already been used up 
for off-city relocation projects...In conclusion, Rep. Villarin said that Congress can push for policies on the building of disaster-resilient 
settlements for urban communities; institutionalization of the DILG´s role in the implementation of the Urban Development and Housing Act of 1992 and relevant laws; funding for a socialized housing finance corporation; and provision of  additional allocations for the ISF resettlement fund. (SOURCE: House Journal No.19,pp.6-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2016-09-14

rows.author: I093;
rows.abstract:
... Rep. Shernee Abubakar Tan rose on a question of privilege to condemn an attempt to open her vehicle in the HOR North Wing parking lot the 
previous day. She said that the PNP...surmised that the culprit had intended to plant explosives under the front seat where she usually sat. She stressed the need to strictly implement security 
measures in the HOR premises ...;stated that the country has been jittery since the recent Davao City bombing and the ongoing intense military operations against the Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG) and that they cannot count out the possibility that the mastermind in the previous night´s incident would ride on the Abu Sayyaf fever and point out the latter as the perpetrators. Kusug Tausug.(SOURCE: House Jounal No.19,p.7)

rows.author: I030;
rows.title_full: BAGUIO, LA TRINIDAD, IITOGON, SUBLAY, TUBA, TUBLAY DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (BLISTTDA)
rows.abstract:
... Rep. Go stressed the need to rehabilitate and ensure the progress of Baguio City and its five adjacent municipalities ... Benguet, La Trinidad, 
Itogon, Sablan, Tuba and Tublay (BLISTT) through 
the creation of a BLISTT Development Authority 
(BLISTTDA)...; explained how a once-clean, cosmopolitan, and uncrowded city had become a jungle of congestion, waste, traffic, informal settlements, and an increasing population due to rapid urbanization without a wellprepared development plan...; said that  he had filed House Bill No. 1554 seeking the creation of the BLISTTDA ...; relayed to the Body the salient and pertinent
provisions of House Bill No. 1554,... stated that the creation of the BLISTTDA offers a road map to bring back the glory days of the said areas adjacent to Baguio City and to achieve a sustainable social and economic growth for the interest and benefit of the people of Baguio City... (House Journal No.20,pp.5-6)

rows.author: I102;
rows.title_full: PROPOSAL FOR HALF-DAY WORK SCHEDULE FOR TEACHERS
rows.abstract:
...Rep. Belaro,...paid homage to the teachers 
whom he described as the unsung heroes for their contributions to nation-building. He stated that through legislation, he wished to give the teachers more time for themselves, for their families as well as their other concerns.  
Pointing out that the teaching profession is not 
only about pedagogy but also involves myriad tasks, he said that he is proposing to look at the problem of low salaries of teachers in a different light considering that it is not just about their salaries but also about the terms and conditions of their work. As such, he then proposed that teachers be allowed to work for half-day only and appealed to his colleagues to support his 
measure... (House Journal No.20,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2016-09-14

rows.author: I080;
rows.title_full: PROBLEM OF CONTRACTUALIZATION
rows.abstract:
Rep. Casilao focused on Party-List Anakpawis´ 
call to seize and stop the practice of labor contractualization that has long began  even before the last presidential campaign. He expressed gladness that no less than President Rodrigo Roa Duterte had promised the abolition of contractualization as he noted that the latter had offered top positions  in the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE)  to the members of the 
Left...; He related that he had manifested to the DOLE Secretary his desire to participate in the deliberations on  the nullification  of DOLE Department Order 18-A, Series of 2011 which he said the capitalists use to perpetuate the practice of labor contractualization...; stressed that he would file a bill providing for a national minimum wage to achieve a unified, national minimum wage, and subsequently touched on House Bill No. 556 or the AntiContractualization Bill. 
...;added that he has also looked into the problem 
of contractualization of House employees and other 
government agencies since his advocacy includes not only workers in private but also in the public sector... (Source: House Journal No.20,pp.6-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2016-09-14
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Erice

rows.author: I066;
rows.title_full: ON-LINE BASHING
rows.abstract:
Rep. Teves spoke on the issue of bashing on social 
media which he had brought up during a committee 
hearing and on the need to regulate the use of social media which does not mean restricting one´s freedom of speech. Even as he has no problem with social bashing, he pointed out that what is more important to him is the identity and ccountability of the social media account holders. In this regard, Rep. Teves signified his intent to 
file a bill, for which he asked his colleagues´ support, requesting social media companies to regulate and filter social media accounts. He added that under his proposed measure, a social media entity which cannot filter a malicious account, may be held equally accountable. He said that he became a victim of social bashing on Facebook recently from a group using the name 
“Nurses for Change Movement” after he suggested a 
ban against grumpy nurses in government hospitals.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.21,p.14)

rows.author: I057;
rows.title_full: BOTTOM UP BUDGETING
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ramon V.A.“RAV” Rocamora ... spoke about the need to continue the past administration´s program on participatory budgeting or bottomup-budgeting (BuB) which is planned to be removed from the proposed 2017 national budget. He expressed 
gladness that many members of the civil society and local government officials spoke in defense of the BuB that eventually convinced the national government to give the program a second look including Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Ismael “Mike” Sueño who agreed to continue the projects that were products of exhaustive discussions and deliberations by communities. He hoped that the DILG will heed the sentiments of the local communities and local government units (LGUs)
which want to continue the program...In view thereof, he said that he had filed House Joint Resolution No. 4 calling for the restoration of the P35 billion allotted fund for BuB in the proposed 2017 national budget and asked the support of Rep. Karlo Alexei B. Nograles, as Chair of the Committee on Appropriations, as well as the Members of the 17th Congress to support the approval of the Joint Resolution.(SOURCE: House Journal No.21,p.14-15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2016-09-21
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep.Villarin

rows.author: I080;
rows.title_full: HUMAN RIGHTS OF FARMERS
rows.title_short: 44th Anniversary Of The Declaration Of Martial Law
rows.abstract:
... Rep. Casilao spoke on the issue of human rights violations particularly on the political and extrajudicial killings of farmers, farmworkers, lumads and indigenous peoples (IPs). He stated that such killings are reminiscent of the martial law era and that the farmers and farmworkers still continue to 
experience such kind of abuse to date...; expressed support on the ongoing formal peace talks between the National Democratic Front of 
the Philippines (NDFP) and the government,...; urged his colleagues to join the clamor for 
the release of some 500 political prisoners and to support House Resolution No.198 filed by the Makabayan Coalition seeking the release of political prisoners...; emphasized the right of farmers to labor on their land in peace, without threat and intimidation, and called for justice for the continuing atrocities of the military against the marginalized sector.(SOURCE: House Journal No. 22,p.11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2016-09-21

rows.author: I106;
rows.title_full: PUERTO PRINCESA : THE GATEWAY TO PALAWAN'S TOURISM HUBS
rows.abstract:
Rep. Acosta ... emphasized how the travel and tourism industry has contributed to the country´s gross domestic product and attracted millions of foreign visitors. He stressed that his province, Palawan, has been in the forefront of tourism boom, and that Puerto Princesa City,...is the gateway thereto, with a multitude of tourist facilities and historical landmarks. He mentioned in particular the Puerto Princesa Underground River which is a UNESCO World Heritage site 
and considered one of the Seven Wonders of Nature,
as well as the El Nido Reserve and the Coron island. Rep. Acosta presented the ff. suggestions to help maximize the tourism potentials of Palawan and the City of Puerto Princesa...: 1) a policy program to expand and intensify secondary attractions and projects that must be supported by the national government; 2) a plan or program to improve infrastructure facilities in Palawan such as a cruise port facility that could cater to tourists and visitors; and 3) a measure 
declaring Palawan as the ecological tourism capital of the Philippines. (SOURCE: House Journal No. 22,pp.11-12)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TOURISM since 2016-09-21

rows.author: I083;
rows.title_full: DECREASE IN THE 2017 BUDGET OF STATE UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES
rows.abstract:
Rep. Elago expressed  her concern regarding the 
deep cuts on the proposed 2017 budget of the CHED, specifically on the proposed budgets for the State universities and colleges (SUCs).  She said that these cuts would again give cause for the administrators of the SUCs to increase their tuition and other expenses thus further 
burdening the students. She likewise expressed her apprehension that State schools might introduce new and higher fees in the coming year just to meet the internal income target...; stated that about 112 of her colleagues had signed a joint statement pushing for a stop to the impending budget cuts...The joint statement, she said, calls on the Cttee. on Appropriations and Members of both Chambers of Congress to immediately stop the impending budget cuts and augment the funding for public tertiary education with the end view of achieving free public education in due time...; urged everyone to join the Youth Action Day for Education and Human Rights on September 21, 2016 to fight for their right to education.(SOURCE: House Journal No.22,pp.14-15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2016-09-21

rows.author: I020;
rows.title_full: PROMOTING THE FILM INDUSTRY IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Rep. De Venecia delved first on the success of the 
film “Ang Babaeng Humayo” or “The Woman Who 
Left” that recently won several awards abroad. In this light, he congratulated the films´s director Lav Diaz who was also its screenwriter, cinematographer, editor and coproducer, for his unparalleled vision, genius and unwavering commitment to his craft. He also commended the actors and producers of Mr. Diaz´ films including those whom he further enumerated. Citing measures promoting Filipino films that Congress passed during the speakership of his father, former Speaker Jose C. De Venecia, he asked the 
Body to pass similar bills filed in the 17th
Congress. He also relayed the advocacies of several art groups and summits for the protection of artists welfare and a Film Archive; and stressed the role of culture in entertainment, social transformation, and economic growth. (SOURCE: House Journal No.22,p.15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2016-09-21

rows.author: H066;
rows.title_full: ADDRESSING BUDGET DEFICIT AND NATIONAL DEBT
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bravo initially discussed the fiscal performance of past administrations starting from President Ferdinand E. Marcos to President Rodrigo Duterte, citing statistics on debts and budget deficits.  He then stressed the need to tackle the vicious cycle of borrowing and spending during the current budget process and pointed out that trillions of pesos are available in the national coffers to address the same as had been stated in the President´s budget message for 2017. He enumerated the government´s unused appropriations and stressed that it had failed to implement 
funded programs as well as asked why it had to resort to borrowings. He proposed that the Committees on Appropriations, and Ways and Means scrutinize how the funds could be used and consider the one-fund concept in government budgeting and accounting. (SOURCE: House Journal No.22,pp.15-16)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2016-09-21
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Alejano and Casilao

rows.author: G101;
rows.title_full: WEATHER INDEX-BASED CROP INSURANCE AND RECAPITALIZATION AND EXPANSION OF THE PHILIPPINE CROP INSURANCE CORPORATION
rows.abstract:
Rep. Yap centered on the defectively designed insurance for agricultural products with the agricultural crop insurance continuing to be peril- or indemnitybased. He said that the inefficiency, tediousness, complexity and attendant hazards in crop insurance which
result in exorbitant and unreasonable premium prices for insurance products make crop insurance in the country very unpopular. However, Rep. Yap pointed out that in other parts of the world such as India, the Carribean and Africa, which are also reeling from the effects of climate change, crop insurance is being offered on the basis of innovative terms, thus, instead of being peril- or indemnity-based, crop insurance in these areas is classified as weather index-based insurance
(WIBI). . . In closing, Rep. Yap sought his colleagues´ support for the recapitalization and expansion of the Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation´s mandate to engage in reinsurance and direct insurance of WIBI products for crops and agriculture. (SOURCE: House Journal No.23,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2016-10-12

rows.author: G064;
rows.title_short: Condemning The Use Of Any Congressional Inquiries And False Witnesses To Discredit The President
rows.abstract:
Rep. Nograles dwelled on the alleged web of lies
claimed by the surprise witness in the hearing on extrajudicial killings of the Senate Committee on Justice. He said that he and his father, former Speaker Prospero Nograles, have come out to dispute the lies told by the surprise witness,. . .  Rep. Nograles also lamented the inconsistencies and distortions of facts and events which have been overlooked; and the surprise witness being heard in a legislative hearing upon the direct endorsement of the
committee chairperson herself. In this light, Rep.
Nograles pointed out that the Senate hearing was not a sincere search for truth on the matter of extrajudicial killings but a calculated and unmitigated direct assault on the dignity and reputation of the President of the Republic. . . He added that at stake is not simply the success on the war against illegal drugs or the agenda for reform of the Duterte Administration
but the stability and survival of the Republic.
In conclusion, Rep. Nograles condemned the lies
to destroy the President´s dignity and reputation and the use of inquiries in aid of legislation for such and asked the Body to be vigilant in defending the truth, justice, and the people´s mandate. (SOURCE: House Journal No.23,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2016-09-19

rows.author: I058;
rows.title_full: DISCRIMINATION BASED ON SEXUAL ORIENTATION AND GENDER IDENTITY
rows.title_short: Sexual Equality And L G B T Rights
rows.abstract:
Rep. Roman initially recalled the support and acceptance that her father, the late Rep. Antonino P. Roman, had given her as a daughter, transgender, and politician. She also thanked the Members of the 17th Congress for welcoming her and treating her with dignity and respect, as had been her father´s dream. Rep. Roman then advocated the needs of lesbians, gays, bisexuals and transgenders (LGBTs), saying she could not turn her back on their plight even as she wanted to focus on serving her constituents as her parents had done before her. She said that the LGBTs had suffered discrimination and had been denied adequate legal protection as she had herself experienced although they were part of society and were human beings; and enumerated their needs such as sociopsychological support and legal and labor protection. Stressing that Congress must immediately pass the Anti-Discrimination Bill, she discussed some features
thereof such as discriminatory acts on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity (SOGI) and the corresponding penalties. . .
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 23,pp.6-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2016-10-12
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Bag-ao, de Venecia, Bagatsing, Villarin, Herrera-Dy, Vergara, Elago, Roa-Puno and Andaya

rows.author: H046;
rows.title_full: STRESSED THE NEED TO STRENGTHEN VOLUNTARY ACCREDITATION AMONG HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS
rows.title_short: Voluntary Accreditation System; Quality Of The Country's Higher Education
rows.abstract:
. . . Rep. Olivarez stressed the need to strengthen voluntary accreditation among higher education institutions (HEIs) in order for the country to cope with global competitiveness.
He cited facts and figures on the number of HEIs in the country and their student population, the low passing rate in licensure examinations,the small percentage of master´s degree-holders among college faculty, and the warning among the business community on the economic impact of inadequately trained and prepared graduates...; also discussed Memo Order No. 1 (2005) of the CHED on the policies and guidelines on accreditation and described what was being
done about accreditation in the context of the ASEAN community...; stated that he would file a measure to strengthen voluntary accreditation in the Philippines by institutionalizing its existing policies and practices and providing financial assistance therefor. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.23,p.15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2016-10-12

rows.author: I108;
rows.title_full: APPEALED TO THE PHILIPPINE SPORTS COMMISSION (PSC) TO CONSIDER THE INCLUSION OF SURFING AS A \"FOCUS SPORT\" AND AS ONE OF THE PRIORITIES FOR ITS GRASSROOTS PROGRAM FOR DEVELOPMENT
rows.title_short: Siargao Islands As The Surfing Capital Of The Philippines
rows.abstract:
Rep. Matugas initially discussed the sport of surfing and its popularity in the island of Siargao which became internationally known as the surfing capital of the Philippines and ranked by many local and international surfers as the best surfing spot in the world. In this regard, he then informed the Body that the island of Siargao would be hosting the 22nd International Surfing Competitions which would determine the qualifiers for the World Surf League world tour. As the International Olympic Committee had announced
that surfing would be included in the 2020
Olympics in Tokyo, Japan, Rep. Matugas expressed
belief that surfing would be the sport where the Philippines can excel and finally earn an Olympic gold medal. As such, he enjoined his colleagues to support the Filipino surfers so they could do well in the qualifying rounds leading to the 2020 Tokyo Olympic and appealed to the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) to consider the inclusion of surfing as a “focus sport” and as one of the priorities for its grassroots program for development....(SOURCE: House Journal No.23,p.15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2016-10-12

rows.author: I010;
rows.title_full: SUCCESSFUL STAGING OF THE PROCESSION OF OUR LADY OF PENAFRANCIA IN NAGA CITY DESPITE THE THREAT OF TERRORISM
rows.title_short: Threat Of Terrorism During The Penafrancia Festival In Naga
rows.abstract:
Describing to the Body ... the street procession in honor of the Our Lady of Peñafrancia ... and dubbed in his region as the festival of festivals due to its sheer breadth and historicity, Rep. Bordado disclosed how this year´s Marian festival had to contend with the shadow of terrorism.  
He thereafter cited a PNP intelligence report that a member of the Abu Sayyaf Group was in Naga City, but that the Joint Operations Center led by the City Government of Naga and the Archdiocese of Caceres, together with the AFP, the PNP as well as other concerned government and NGOs had reassured the public that everything was under control and that proactive steps were being taken to address the threat of terrorism. Thus, the nineday Peñafrancia festivities successfully proceeded without any terroristic act, he added. He expressed belief that the Joint Operations Center was worth replicating in other areas of the country and said that with the outpouring of faith, hope and love, the Peñafrancia festival will always be a source of strength and inspiration for people in quest of peace for a strife-torn world. (SOURCE: House Journal No.24,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2016-10-12

rows.author: H081;
rows.title_full: SUPPORTED PRESIDENT DUTERTE'S INDEPENDENT FOREIGN POLICY
rows.abstract:
... Rep. Carlos Isagani T. Zarate... spoke in 
Filipino to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the removal of US military bases in Subic and 
Clark through the so-called “Magnificent 12 Senators” and at the same time, to point out that America´s domination over the Philippines has continued through the operation of the VFA) and the EDCA, as well as the existence of neoliberal policies that disproportionately favor the US causing damage to the national economy and the Filipino citizens. Rep. Zarate however believed that hope remains for the patriotic Filipinos in light of President Rodrigo Roa Duterte´s statements in the past few days on the dismissal of US military troops in Mindanao; in exposing the massacre by US military troops of Moros in Bud Dajo and the Samareños in Balangiga; and his 
rejection of a joint patrol in the West Philippines Sea. He maintained that the President´s statements and proposals for an independent foreign policy will surely benefit the country and its people. Thereafter, Rep. Zarate stated that the present Administration should push for the country´s exclusive economic zone and continental shelf in accordance with the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea and that an independent foreign policy to succeed requires 
the collective action of the citizenry, a strong political will, and an aggressive rejection of neocolonialism and US domination. (House Journal No.24,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOREIGN AFFAIRS since 2016-10-12

rows.author: I081;
rows.title_full: LOW SALARIES OF TEACHERS
rows.title_short: Achievements, Concerns And Priorities Of Teachers
rows.abstract:
Rep. Castro took the floor to recognize the crucial role of teachers in society; to explain the history and rationalÃ© behind the celebration of World Teachers Day on Oct.5 each year since 1996;and to discuss the UNESCO-ILO recommendations adopted in 1966 addressing several issues on the plight of teachers, such as professionalism, teacher training, and professional freedom. 
Thereafter, the Lady Member talked about teaching being regarded as a profession and a form of public service which requires expertise, knowledge and specialized skills that are acquired and maintained through rigorous and continuous study. She then delved into the issue of the low salaries being paid to teachers in the country. After proposing to limit the class sizes to 35 students per class, Rep. Castro asked the Body to pass HB No.56 and other measures for the increase in teachers´ salaries to decent and realistic levels because EO No. 201 provided for a very small salary increase. (SOURCE: House Journal No.24,p.11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2016-10-12
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Belaro

rows.author: G001;
rows.title_full: ROLE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS IN THE OVERALL SCHEME OF PRESERVING PEACE AND ORDER AS WELL AS GUARANTEEING PUBLIC SAFETY
rows.title_short: Role Of Local Government Units In Preserving Peace And Order And Guaranteeing Public Safety In The Campaign Against Lawlessness And Violence
rows.abstract:
Rep. Acharon underlined the significance of the 
Duterte government´s campaign against lawless violence and terrorism in the country and highlighted the role of LGUs in the overall 
scheme of preserving peace and order as well as guaranteeing public safety. As the spate of bombings in Mindanao may appear to be isolated cases, he stated however that these violent acts are continuous and the magnitude of violence and damages to lives and property are proportionate to the prevailing crisis at hand. As he cited several acts of terrorism in Mindanao... Rep. Acharon stressed that a sustainable campaign for a more exceptional level of public order and safety needs the proactive cooperation of every Filipino citizen as well as the support of LGUs...; pointed out that R.A. No.6975 or the DILG Act of 1990 clearly established the policy ... As he fully supports the ongoing war on drugs and campaign against lawlessness, Rep. Acharon stated that the government must also address the acts of terrorism that is continuously being carried out with impunity... (SOURCE: House Journal No.24,p.12)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2016-10-12

rows.author: H066;
rows.title_full: URGED CONGRESS TO EXERCISE ITS OVERSIGHT FUNCTIONS OVER THE UTILIZATION OF THE MOTOR VEHICLE USER'S CHARGE (MVUC) FUND
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bravo expressed concern on issues surrounding the Motor Vehicle User´s Charge (MVUC) Fund 
by first stressing that it is the third largest source of tax revenue in the country,... explaining its implementing rules and regulations which mandated the establishment of the Road Board, the DPWH Road Program and the DOTC Vehicle Pollution Control Fund Committee. He also cited the role of the Land Transportation Officer in the collection of MVUC Fund; the amount collected from 2004 to 2015 and where it was utilized; the reports and findings of the COA on the irregularities, misuse, improper and 
unliquidated use of the funds; the status of the implementation of the seven programmed infrastructure projects of the Road Board Secretariat for 2016; the COA report regarding the 2015 MVUC auditing; and the reason for the suspension and delay of projects under the National Road Lighting Program (NRLP)...Rep. Bravo expressed apprehension that a huge part of the fund is lost to graft and corruption. To exact transparency in the utilization of the MVUC Fund, he urged Congress to exercise its oversight functions over the fund and to scrutinize the expenditures of the DPWH) and DOTr), relative to its utilization so as to stop further wastage of public funds. (SOURCE: House Journal No.24,pp.14-15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2016-10-12
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Batocabe

rows.author: I062;
rows.title_full: AS A RESULT OF THE DEATH OF HIS DRIVER, WHILE WAITING INSIDE HIS CAR, HE PROPOSED THAT THE HOUSE PROVIDE THEM WITH A LOUNGE WHERE THEY CAN STAY AND WAIT
rows.title_short: Call On House Officials And The Lsb To Ensure Safety And Security In All Areas Of The House
rows.abstract:
Rep. Sarmiento talked about the unfortunate incident that happened...that caused the life 
of his personal driver...; believed that his driver was poisoned by carbon monoxide as the car was accidentally parked close to the gutter with the exhaust muffler and pipe obstructed by
soil. Whereupon, Rep. Sarmiento stated that he considers the staff members in the House of Representatives,... as the unsung heroes behind their legislative and district work, and that each and every one of them is indispensable to their work...; called on the House Officials, especially the Legislative Security Bureau, to impose more stringent patrolling protocols, to include car idling in excess of  30 minutes to ensure the safety and security in all areas of the House...; proposed that they be provided with a lounge where they can stay and wait until the adjournment of each session. (SOURCE: House Journal No.24,p.15)

rows.author: G053;
rows.title_full: ILLEGAL DRUG TRADE IN HIS DISTRICT
rows.abstract:
Rep. Jalosjos rose to expose anew certain personalities in his province which he alleged are involved in the illegal drug trade...lamented however that the illegal drug trade in his province still continues because it is protected by certain police officials and narco-politicians.  
He then presented to the Body a drug matrix identifying the names of the drug lord inmates in the Dipolog City Jail, the drug protectors, the drug operations and activities, and the money trail. He stated that these drug lords are under the protection of SPO2 Roy P. Vertudes who directly coordinates with operators and handlers of the illegal drug trade. He then explained why SPO2 Vertrudes has remained “untouchable” in his province ... He disclosed that in one murder case filed against SPO2 Vertudes in 2015, then Justice Sec. Leila de Lima intervened in his behalf by issuing a department order. With respect to reports that the Dipolog City Port is being used for illegal drugs operations, Rep. Jalosjos said that there is already an existing port in Dapitan City which is only a stone´s throw away from the former. He asked why the Dipolog City Port was created,  and why it was being run by a LGU that was not authorized by the PPA and not under the jurisdiction of the Phil. Coast Guard Auxiliary... He said that he was  also a victim of an assassination plot during the campaign period and lamented that the PNP has not acted on his case, this as he opined that SPO2 Vertudes and his 
cohorts have remained untouched because of their 
protector, and asked for their immediate investigation...he asked for the replacement of the PNP Provincial Director, NBI Provincial Director and PDEA Provincial Chief assigned in his province. He also recommended the investigation of and filing of charges against the DILG and DOJ officials in the previous Administration because of gross neglect of duty and giving of undue favors.(SOURCE: House Journal No.25,pp.11-12)

rows.author: H065;
rows.title_full: WARNED AGAINST THE GRANTING OF EMERGENCY POWERS TO THE PRESIDENT TO SOLVE THE TRAFFIC PROBLEM
rows.abstract:
Citing the experience of the country and lessons 
that the Filipino learned when the late President Ferdinand E. Marcos declared martial law on September 21, 1972, Rep. Atienza reminded the Body that the Philippines as a nation has been blessed with rich and abundant land and that the only thing the Filipinos need is a leader who would govern and inspire them and not to curtail their human rights.  He said that giving emergency powers to one man will never work to the advantage of the people nor would this improve their lives but would only deprive the people of their 
freedom inasmuch as no opposition would be able to 
check or speak against the abuses of the government. He then cited, among others, the experience of previous Philippine presidents who were granted emergency powers in order to change the form of government or to abet the looming energy crisis.  He opined that President Duterte´s effort alone will not succeed even if Congress granted him emergency powers to solve the country´s traffic problem because it can only be solved by a united effort of the LGUs, law enforcement agencies, and the people in general.  
He opined that the traffic issue should not be used as an excuse to undermine the nation´s democracy. He then called on the Members to remember the lessons of martial law and the emergency powers granted to the revolutionary government of former President Cory Aquino...
(SOURCE: House Journal No.25,pp.12-13)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2016-10-12
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Tambunting, Bordado, Mercado and Acosta.
